title: Fast Walking Helps Health, Even Below 10,000 Steps
paragraphs: Walking is great exercise that doesn't require a gym membership or any equipment beyond some comfortable shoes.

A lot of walking apps encourage people to aim for around 10,000 steps a day. But new research suggests that taking fewer steps at a faster pace can lower your risk of early death about as well as taking more steps at a slower pace.

A study published in the British Journal of Sports Medicine looked at data from around 100,000 middle-aged people living in the UK. Participants wore an activity tracker to count their daily steps for seven consecutive days between 2013 and 2015.

Participants' step counts were divided into four categories: zero to 5,000 steps per day, 5,000 to 7,500 steps, 7,500 to 10,000 steps, and over 10,000 steps per day. The researchers also calculated each person's fastest sustained stepping rate during the most active half hour of the day.
The researchers then looked at how many participants died before the end of November 2022, and compared death rates with walking patterns.

They found that people who took fewer than 5,000 steps a day still had a far lower risk of death if they also achieved a higher stepping pace of at least 80 steps per minute. This group got the same benefits from walking as those who took between 5,000 and 7,500 steps a day at a pace of around 60 steps per minute.

In fact, keeping a fast pace for at least 30 minutes a day was linked to a lower risk of death no matter how many steps people took. However, taking 7,500 to 10,000 steps a day, at any pace, was still linked to the lowest risk of early death.
Still, these results may be helpful for people who don't have the time or space — or just aren't healthy enough — to take a full 10,000 steps a day.
